orbit.title: The radar dancing over Cochabamba
orbit.intro: NISAR circles the Earth every ~100 minutes and repeats the same orbit every 12 days. Its radar sees through clouds and at night, so it can track water, soil and terrain in our basins all year round.
orbit.disclaimerPosition: Position computed from public orbital elements (TLE) with the SGP4 model. This is not live telemetry.
orbit.disclaimerPass: A predicted orbital pass does not guarantee that NISAR acquires an image: that depends on its observation plan.
orbit.disclaimerSwath: The swath is illustrative: the real radar looks sideways, not straight down.
orbit.tleStale: Orbital elements are more than {{days}} days old: the position may be inaccurate.
orbit.error: Could not get the NISAR orbit
orbit.pendingCatalog: Will appear once the backend catalog is available.
